§1.2 Conformance

📚 Document rule — needs other pages of the document; decided once and applied on every page

conventions-conformance · conventions

✅ Normative

A conforming output is a Markdown rendering of a document that satisfies every MUST of this protocol, optionally accompanied by a sidecar that satisfies The Sidecar§3.4. A producer conforms when every output it emits conforms.

What is judged

An output is judged against the document as rendered — the pages a reader sees — and never against the file's text layer, OCR, or another output. See The Page Is the Ground Truth§2.1.

Part Required Governed by
Markdown always Markdown Rendering§3.2 and chapters 4–13
Sidecar when boxes are requested The Sidecar§3.4, Boxes and Granularity§3.3

Verdicts

A check of an output against the protocol yields findings, each tied to one requirement:

  • a violated MUST is an error; any error makes the output non-conforming;
  • a violated SHOULD is a warning; warnings do not affect conformance;
  • a requirement marked ❓ open yields warnings only, whatever its keyword, until it is settled.

Equivalent forms

Where the protocol accepts more than one rendering (⚖️), every accepted rendering conforms, and a consumer MUST treat them as equal. A document MUST NOT mix accepted renderings of the same situation — see Choices Made Once Per Document§4.2 and Accepted Alternatives§A.1.

Output options

A few requirements depend on what the producer was asked to produce, such as whether table fragments are joined across pages. They are listed in Output Options§3.5; an output is judged under the options it was produced with.

Related

  • Requirements Language§1.1 — the meaning of MUST, SHOULD and MAY
  • Output Options§3.5 — requirements that depend on the producer's settings
  • Accepted Alternatives§A.1 — renderings that are equal for conformance
